Subject: Prostate Multiparametric MRI / Date: 20 January 2025 / Facility: Amsterdam UMC (location AMC)

Clinical Context: PSA value: 7.9 ng/mL alongside routine monitoring.

Observations: The prostate volume: 43.67 mL. A discrete abnormality, roughly 18 mm at its largest, resides in the posterior segment of the left peripheral zone. T2 sequences show a sharply hypointense region with poorly defined borders. Diffusion-weighted scans highlight marked restriction, mirrored by suppressed ADC values. Post-contrast dynamics exhibit prompt, localized uptake compared to adjacent tissue. Capsular integrity remains intact without seminal vesicle involvement. Pelvic nodes show normal dimensions and structure.

Impression: PI-RADS: 5 lesion in the left posterior peripheral zone, measuring approximately 18 mm. PSA density: 0.181 ng/mL/mL. csPCa probability: 0.86869615.

previous_notes.author: Dr. N. Kuiper (GP)
previous_notes.text: During a visit on 06 Feb 2023, Dr. N. Kuiper assessed the patient after his PSA climbed to 4.6 ng/mL. A subsequent blood draw was booked, with instructions to return if readings kept rising. Moderate lower urinary tract symptoms were recorded, alongside a decision to track the trajectory over the next few months.
